meta.titre: The Five Pillars of Islam: faith, worship, charity and community
meta.sous_theme: Shahada, Salat, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj, and what they say about Muslim unity
tags: A Level Religious Studies - five pillars of islam

source.epreuve_titre: GCE A/L Religious Studies past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: Muslim communities across Cameroon, from the markets of Douala to the towns of the North, mark the month of Ramadan with pre-dawn meals, sunset meals shared with neighbours and a joyful festival at the end. These habits come from five duties that Muslims call the pillars of Islam. At A Level the examiners do not only ask you to name them: they ask what each one means, how Muslims practise it, and how the pillars together bind believers into one community. Paper 1 tests the definitions and Paper 2 tests your ability to comment and to link one pillar with another.

items: Muslims are the followers of Islam, which they believe was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad as the final message from God.
Allah is the Arabic name for God, and the Quran is the holy book of Islam.
Makkah (Mecca) in Arabia is the holiest city of Islam and contains the Kaaba, towards which Muslims face in prayer.

sections.titre: The five pillars (arkan al-Islam) and the unity they express
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The five pillars
| Pillar | Meaning | Main features |
|---|---|---|
| Shahada | Testimony of faith | The declaration that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the messenger of Allah. Said sincerely, it marks entry into Islam, and it is repeated in the call to prayer and in the daily prayers. |
| Salat | Ritual prayer | Five set times each day (Fajr at dawn, Zuhr at midday, Asr in the afternoon, Maghrib at sunset, Isha at night), facing Makkah, after ritual washing (wudu). The midday prayer on Friday is said in congregation in the mosque after a sermon. |
| Zakat | Almsgiving | The obligatory yearly giving of a fixed share of qualifying wealth to the poor and to other groups named in Islamic teaching. Muslims understand it as purifying both the wealth and the giver. |
| Sawm | Fasting | Throughout Ramadan, the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, adult Muslims abstain from food and drink from dawn to sunset. The sick, travellers and young children are among those exempted. The month ends with the festival of Eid al-Fitr. |
| Hajj | Pilgrimage | A journey to Makkah in the month of Dhu al-Hijjah, required once in a lifetime of every Muslim who is physically and financially able. Its rites include wearing the simple garments of ihram, walking around the Kaaba (tawaf) and standing at Arafat. |

Do not confuse these five duties with the articles of faith (iman), which are beliefs such as belief in God, angels, scriptures, prophets and the Last Day.

### How the pillars show unity and solidarity
- **Shahada**: one short creed, recited in Arabic by Muslims of every nation, race and language.
- **Salat**: all face the same direction, and in congregation worshippers stand side by side in rows and make the same movements, in principle without regard to wealth or rank.
- **Zakat**: wealth moves from the better off to the needy, so that each Muslim shares responsibility for the welfare of others.
- **Sawm**: rich and poor feel the same hunger and thirst, which builds sympathy, and the evening meals and Eid are shared.
- **Hajj**: pilgrims from all over the world gather at the same places, perform the same rites and wear similar plain clothing, which expresses equality before God.

### Answering 'identify and comment'
Identify means name and describe briefly; comment means add an explanation or evaluation. For each pillar chosen, write a three-part paragraph: name it, say what Muslims do, then state the unity or solidarity it produces.

variantes.nom: Question on the link between two pillars
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for the link or relationship between two pillars, usually for 5 marks.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give a similarity and a difference. For Salat and Zakat: both are compulsory acts of worship, both are understood to purify (the soul and the wealth), both remind believers that everything belongs to God, and Islamic teaching often mentions them together. They differ in that Salat is directed mainly towards God while Zakat is directed towards fellow human beings, so together they join duty to God and duty to the community.

variantes.nom: Objective question on the Shahada and the other pillars
variantes.quand_utiliser: In Paper 1 when a single word or phrase is required.
variantes.contenu_markdown: The testimony of faith is the Shahada; the prayer is Salat; almsgiving is Zakat; fasting is Sawm; pilgrimage is Hajj. Match the description with the Arabic term and eliminate options that belong to another pillar.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain how the Hajj and the fast of Ramadan help to build a sense of community among Muslims. (12 marks)

etapes.action: Analyse the command word and key terms.
etapes.justification: 'Explain how' asks for a cause and effect link, not a description alone; the key idea is community (the ummah).
etapes.resultat_markdown: Two pillars: Hajj and Sawm. Each needs a practice and an effect on community.

etapes.justification: A plan keeps the answer balanced and prevents a list.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Short introduction, paragraph on Hajj, paragraph on Sawm, short conclusion.

etapes.action: Write the Hajj paragraph with evidence.
etapes.justification: Evidence of practice shows knowledge; the link shows understanding.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Pilgrims from many nations perform the same rites in the same places and wear simple plain garments, so differences of wealth and nationality are set aside.

etapes.action: Write the Sawm paragraph with evidence.
etapes.justification: A second pillar with its own practice and effect earns the remaining marks.
etapes.resultat_markdown: All adult Muslims who are able fast from dawn to sunset, share hunger and thirst, break the fast together and celebrate Eid al-Fitr, which builds sympathy for the poor and a shared rhythm of life.

etapes.justification: A conclusion answers the question asked.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Both pillars turn private devotion into shared experience, so they strengthen the sense of belonging to one community.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer.** The Hajj and Ramadan both create community because they are shared experiences. In the Hajj, Muslims from many countries travel to Makkah in the month of Dhu al-Hijjah and perform the same rites, such as walking around the Kaaba and standing at Arafat. Wearing the plain garments of ihram, they appear alike, which Muslims understand as showing equality before God and the unity of the ummah. In Ramadan, adult Muslims who are able fast from dawn to sunset. Because rich and poor alike go hungry and thirsty, believers feel sympathy for those in need, and the evening meals taken together and the festival of Eid al-Fitr strengthen family and neighbourhood bonds. In conclusion, both pillars turn individual obedience into a common experience, and so they build a strong sense of belonging to one worldwide community.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing the five pillars when asked to 'comment' on three of them.
items.pourquoi_faux: Comment requires explanation or evaluation, so a list earns only the identification marks.
items.correction_markdown: Name each chosen pillar, describe the practice, and state the unity or solidarity that it expresses.

items.erreur_markdown: Calling belief in angels or in the Last Day a pillar of Islam.
items.pourquoi_faux: These belong to the articles of faith (iman), not to the five pillars, which are acts of worship.
items.correction_markdown: State the pillars as Shahada, Salat, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj, and treat the articles of faith separately.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that every Muslim must make the Hajj regardless of health or means.
items.pourquoi_faux: The obligation applies to those who are physically and financially able.
items.correction_markdown: Write that the Hajj is required once in a lifetime for those who are able.

items.erreur_markdown: Confusing the Shahada with the five daily prayers.
items.pourquoi_faux: The Shahada is the declaration of faith; the prayers are Salat.
items.correction_markdown: Define the Shahada as the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is his messenger.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing as a believer, for example 'Islam is the only true way'.
items.pourquoi_faux: Examiners expect a neutral, descriptive answer.
items.correction_markdown: Use phrases such as 'Muslims believe' and 'according to Islamic teaching'.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the five pillars of Islam and state in one sentence what the Shahada declares.
items.solution_markdown: The five pillars are **Shahada, Salat, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj**. The Shahada declares that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the messenger of Allah.

items.enonce_markdown: Outline two ways in which the Friday congregational prayer expresses the unity of Muslims. (6 marks)
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for any two points developed: (1) worshippers gather in the mosque and stand side by side in rows, in principle without regard to wealth or rank, which shows equality (up to 3 marks); (2) everyone faces the same direction towards Makkah, follows the same prayer led by the imam and hears the same sermon, which shows a common faith and purpose (up to 3 marks). **Two developed points, 3 marks each.**

items.enonce_markdown: Discuss the view that Zakat is more than a tax on wealth. (15 marks)
items.solution_markdown: Plan: for the view, Zakat is an act of worship done with the intention of obeying God, Muslims understand it as purifying wealth and the giver, it is one of the five pillars and is linked with Salat, and it fosters generosity and solidarity. Against, or qualifying: it is compulsory, it is calculated as a share of wealth held above a minimum, it is redistributive like a tax, and in some countries the state collects it. Evaluation: Muslims distinguish it from a state tax by its religious motive and by the categories of people to whom it is given, although its social effect is similar. **Conclusion: Zakat is both an act of worship and a means of social support, so the view is largely justified.** Award marks for balance, accurate knowledge and a reasoned judgement.

items_markdown: The five pillars are Shahada, Salat, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj; learn the Arabic term and the practice of each.
The Shahada states that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is his messenger.
Unity: one creed, one direction of prayer, wealth shared with the needy, a shared fast, and a pilgrimage in which all wear plain clothes.
Salat and Zakat are linked as worship of God and service of people, and both are understood as purifying.
The pillars are not the same as the articles of faith (iman).
'Identify and comment': name, describe, then explain the effect; stay neutral and write 'Muslims believe'.
